title: Values and loops in Ruby
summary: Use dynamic values, a block, and a condition to count positives.

scenario.briefing: A campus report counts positive stock changes in Ruby.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Count positives in a new array with a predicate.

hints: The each loop already visits every value.
Ask each integer whether it is positive.
Add count += 1 if value.positive? inside the block.

misconceptions.description: Counting zero as a positive change.
misconceptions.testDescription: The block counts only positive values.
misconceptions.feedback: Integer#positive? requires a value greater than zero. Zero and negative values both fail it.

misconceptions.description: Assuming nil responds to every method.
misconceptions.feedback: nil is an object, but most methods are not defined on it. Check for nil or use a safe navigation pattern.

misconceptions.description: Treating a symbol as the same object as a string.
misconceptions.feedback: Symbols are immutable interned names. They are not the same object as a mutable string with the same text.

misconceptions.description: Counting every array element instead of the positive ones.
misconceptions.feedback: count with a block counts only elements that make the block true. Array#size counts every element.

sections.title: Ruby values are dynamic
sections.body: A Ruby local name can hold any object. Integers, floats, strings, symbols, arrays, and hashes all carry their own methods, and the same name can be rebound to a different type later. Symbols are immutable names such as :ready and are commonly used as hash keys.

sections.title: Blocks describe iteration
sections.body: A block is a chunk of behavior passed to a method, written with do/end or braces. The each method yields each element, and the block decides what to do with it. A predicate such as positive? answers a yes-or-no question about one value.

vocabulary.definition: A chunk of code passed to a method, written with do/end or braces.
An immutable name such as :ready, often used as a hash key.
A language where a name can hold values of different types over time.

steps.title: Values and blocks
hints: A Ruby name can be rebound to another type.
Symbol is not the same object as String.
each yields each element to a block.
nil does not accept arbitrary methods.

statements.label: A Ruby variable can be rebound to a value of another type.
A symbol is the same object as a mutable string with the same text.
A block can be yielded to by a method.
Calling a method on nil always returns nil.

steps.explanation: Ruby resolves method calls at runtime. Symbols are immutable names, and nil is an object that does not silently accept every method.

steps.title: Count with a predicate
steps.prompt: Given [4, 0, -3, 7].count { |value| value.positive? }, what is the result?
hints: The block answers a yes-or-no question per element.
The negative value is not positive either.

quiz.prompt: Given [4, 0, -3, 7].count { |value| value.positive? }, what is the result?

options.label: 0, because count only works on ranges

quiz.explanation: Array#count with a block increments only when the block returns true. The values 4 and 7 are positive.
